title: extract
text:
Search finds documents. This page covers what is in them.
A doctype is the type of a document, such as an invoice, a receipt, a contract, a paper, meeting notes or a passport. There are 31 doctypes. The doctype is separate from the document’s kind, which records how the document arrived (web, pdf, note and so on).
The doctype decides two things. It decides the schema that extract uses, which is the list of fields that extract asks a model for. An invoice schema has a number, a vendor, a total and line items. It also decides the shelf that reshelf moves the document to.
varga holds the cue table that recognises each doctype, the schemas, and the code that makes a model answer in the form of a schema. This page stores the varga verdicts in the vault. It runs extraction through the vault’s model and its privacy checks.
categorize decides the doctype of a document and writes it into the document’s meta.
categorize first scores the document against the varga cue table. The cues are phrases such as “invoice no” or “total due”, amounts of money, dates and organisation names. score is the score of the winning doctype. decisive is True when the winning score is clearly higher than the runner-up.
categorize asks a model only when the cues are not decisive. llm= sets this:
With llm='auto', a model error leaves the cue verdict in place, and by names the error type. With llm='always', categorize raises the error.
The model receives the document’s title and text through send_check. A hosted model receives the title and text of a private document masked, or not at all. A file read off disk is judged on its name as well as its text. by says how the verdict was reached.
When the cues are decisive, or a model gave the verdict, categorize writes it as doctype. An undecided verdict with a score of at least REVIEW_SCORE (0.2) is only proposed. categorize writes it as doctype_proposed, and a person confirms it. proposed_types lists the proposals, surest first. accept_type, accept_types and reject_type settle them. suggest_noisy and accept_noisy use the same two-step review for noise.
Below 0.2, categorize writes nothing. reshelf never moves a document on a proposal. categorize_all types every untyped document on the shelf.

title: extract
text:
Extraction
extract reads a whole document, up to max_chars, and returns its fields as a dict.
Without a schema, extract categorises the document first and uses the schema of its doctype. An invoice uses Invoice. A doctype with no schema of its own uses Summary. A schema can also be a SCHEMAS key, a dataclass, or a string such as 'vendor:str, total:float'.
The model answers in the form of the schema through a tool call, a grammar or parsed JSON. The backend decides which of the three is used.
check=True reads every value back through check_fields. errors lists the values that did not fit. src gives the page and block that each field was read from. cite=True adds the quote.
extract_all(doctype='invoice') runs over every invoice and returns one row per document.
Privacy works as in ask, with pii='local' as the default here. send_check makes the decision:

A private document is read by the local pii_model or by no model.
redact masks the title, source and text of a private document for a hosted model.
refuse reads nothing.
A Local only document goes to no hosted model under any policy, off included.
A model on this machine reads the document whole.

extract writes each hosted send to the send log. It scans and masks the fields read from a private document before it returns or saves them.


source

    doctype:str=None, # only documents already categorised as this
    kind:str=None, # only these KINDS

    limit:int=None, # stop after this many
    **kw
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict: # forwarded to extract (model=, chat_kw=, max_chars=, save=, sp=)
Run extract over many documents, such as every invoice, and return one row per document and a list of errors.

def extract(
    ref:str, # doc_id, source, title substring, or a path on disk
    schema:NoneType=None, # a SCHEMAS key, a dataclass, or a 'field:type, …' spec; None -> from the doctype
    model:str=None, # an id, a path, `mlx/…`; None -> $VISHALAKSHI_MODEL
    chat_kw:dict=None, # anything else Urai's `Chat` takes: temp, runtime, think, …
    max_chars:int=8000, # chars of the document the model sees
    sp:str='You pull structured fields out of one document.\n\nRules:\n- Copy what the document states. Do not compute, convert, round or tidy a value.\n- A field the document does not state stays empty. An invented number is worse than a blank one.\n- Numbers are bare: 1240.50, not "$1,240.50". The currency belongs in its own field.\n- Dates are ISO: 2024-03-01.\n- A list field takes every entry the document has, in the order it has them.', # system prompt for the extraction
    save:bool=False, # write the fields into the document's meta
    llm:str='auto', # the LLM leg of the categorisation, when picking the schema
    pii:str='local', # local|redact|refuse|off, as in `ask`; a Local only document reaches no hosted model even under `off`
    pii_model:str=None, # local model when private; None -> $VISHALAKSHI_PII_MODEL
    check:bool=True, # read the values back through `check_fields` and report what did not
    cite:bool=False, # ask for the quote each value was read from; `src` carries it
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
Pull structured fields out of one document, such as an invoice’s number, vendor and totals, in the shape of a schema.

ask_doc(ref, question) is ask with ref=. The document is section [1], whole up to max_chars. related sections from the rest of the vault follow it. schema= returns the answer as fields instead of prose. The privacy rules are the rules of ask.

What retrieval actually returns
v.context(q) is the retrieval that ask uses. It returns whole sections. Each section has a breadcrumb and a node_id that read opens again.
The first cell below prints the length and breadcrumb of each section in results. The code hits at the end come from kosha and ripgrep, because this repository is indexed.

c = v.context('why are rankings fused instead of distances?', sections=4, related=4)
for s in c.results: print(f'{len(s.text):5}  {s.breadcrumb}')

results are the sections that answer the question. related are the sections nearest to them in vector space. They give leads before you know what to search for. They do not change the ranking of results. The via field of each related section says how it was reached.

'minishlab/potion-multilingual-128M (256d, float16, model2vec)'


c.encoder names the embedding model that produced the vectors. With offline=True, the vault hashes character sequences and uses no model. evals/encoder.py measures the cost of this against the default.

title: concepts
text:
Models and backends
A model id names a model. Rishi works out which backend runs it. The local backends are LiteRT, MLX, llama.cpp and Ollama. A hosted API needs its API key. LiteRT is the default local backend.
Rishi owns the backends and their options. They change with Rishi. This page shows only the two arguments that the vault passes on: model= and chat_kw=.

import rishi.core
from urai import Chat, infer_runtime
from vishalakshi.ask import dflt_model

# Rishi names and registers the backends. Urai resolves their model ids.
gemma4_e2b = 'litert-community/gemma-4-E2B-it-litert-lm'
dflt_model, gemma4_e2b     # $VISHALAKSHI_MODEL if set, else the small local default


{m: infer_runtime(m) for m in (gemma4_e2b, 'mlx-community/Qwen3-4B-4bit', 'my-local.gguf',
                               'gpt-5.6-luna', 'gemma-3-4b-it-int4')}


v.ask('why are rankings fused?', model=gemma4_e2b)             # an id: rishi knows what runs it
v.ask('why are rankings fused?', model='llama/my-local.gguf')  # a prefix when the id cannot say
v.ask('why are rankings fused?', model='mlx-community/Qwen3-4B-4bit',
      chat_kw=dict(temp=0, think=True))          # the rest of rishi's constructor


from fastcore.test import test_fail
# `model=` plus `chat_kw=` is the model API. Urai reports an id that names no registered backend.
test_fail(lambda: Chat('gemma-3-4b-it-int4'), contains='backend')

A reasoning model writes its reasoning in a <think> block before the answer. ask puts that block in r.thinking and the rest in r.answer. The block often mentions sections that the model then sets aside. cited reads citations from the answer only.
Retrieval never needs the network. Only answering with a hosted model does.

title: concepts
text:
Encoders
An encoder, or embedding model, turns text into a vector. Texts with similar meanings get vectors that are close together.
The default encoder is a static multilingual model. It produces 256 numbers per text, stored as 16-bit floats.
offline=True hashes character sequences instead. This needs no download. It matches spelling and not meaning.
A shelf records the encoder that wrote it.

Vault(':memory:', offline=True).enc.note      # never attempt a download; also the CI default

'char-n-gram hashing (256d): lexical only; pass encoder= or restore network access for real semantics'



Vault(encoder='minishlab/potion-science-32M')   # pick a different one

Vault('/Users/71293/.vishalakshi/vault.db': 0 docs, 0 chunks, 0 entities, encoder=model2vec)


16-bit floats are the default width in litesearch. One vector index holds the vectors of one encoder. Documents embedded by different encoders need different shelves.
ENCODERS maps three aliases to model ids:

use

The default.


code
The model that kosha uses for identifiers.


gemma
The slowest and most faithful.



Any other model2vec id also works by name.

from vishalakshi.core import ENCODERS

ENCODERS

A static model is a lookup table from words to vectors. It embeds a document in milliseconds without a GPU.
Weighted mean reciprocal rank (MRR) measures how highly retrieval places relevant results. Higher scores are better. litesearch measured weighted MRR across four encoders (evals/encoder.py).

import numpy as np
from vishalakshi.core import mk_encoder

class Eight:
    def encode(self, xs, **kw): return np.zeros((len(xs), 8), dtype=np.float16)

One vector index is one vector space. Different encoders need different shelves. SHELVES names the shelves that the vault uses itself. KIND_SHELF maps each kind that acquisition adds to its own shelf.

from vishalakshi.core import SHELVES, KIND_SHELF

SHELVES, KIND_SHELF

papers.add('# Late chunking\n\nWe evaluate contextual chunk embeddings on BEIR.', 'a paper')

[(s['store'], s['encoder'], s['docs']) for s in v.shelves()]

KIND_SHELF routes documents as they arrive. reshelf moves a document later, when its doctype is known. elsewhere searches the other shelves.

v.route('arxiv').name, v.route('web').name

('papers', 'store')


A PDF may be an invoice or a paper. Its kind does not say which. categorize decides after the document is filed. reshelf then moves the document to the shelf of its doctype.

v.add('# Attention is all you need\n\n## Abstract\n\nWe propose the Transformer.\n\n'
      '## Introduction\n\nRelated work [1] et al.\n\n## References\n\ndoi:10.1/x',
      'attention', source='/inbox/attention.pdf')

r = v.reshelf('/inbox/attention.pdf', llm='never')
r.doctype, r.was, r.store, r.moved

('paper', 'store', 'papers', True)



v.doc('/inbox/attention.pdf'), v.shelf('papers').doc('/inbox/attention.pdf')['title']

(None, 'attention')


Moving a document adds it to the new shelf from scratch. The encoder of the new shelf makes the vectors again. reshelf deletes the copy on the old shelf.
The meta of the document moves with it. It includes the doctype and the shelf that the document came from.
Marks do not move. A mark belongs to a document on its own shelf.
federate runs a search on each shelf. It merges the results by rank, together with the kosha and ripgrep results. elsewhere adds a few sections from the neighbouring shelves to context and ask.

v.federate('contextual chunk embeddings', repo=False, grep=False).legs

{'prose': 3, 'shelf:papers': 4}


Each row from elsewhere has a store field that names its shelf. Pass store to read(node_id, store=...) when the section is not on the current shelf.

e = v.elsewhere('contextual chunk embeddings')
L(e).map(lambda r: (r.store, r.breadcrumb))

[('papers', 'papers › a paper'),

'# Late chunking\n\nWe evaluate contextual chunk embeddings on BEIR.'


A shelf records the encoder that wrote it and reopens with the same encoder. Opening a shelf with a different encoder raises an error, so two vector spaces never mix. To change the encoder of a shelf, drop the shelf and add its documents again.

title: proof
text:
A vision model’s reading of a page can contain slips. Other models, called readers on this page, can read the same pages again and compare their readings with the stored text. Each difference is filed as a change. A change is a run of words to replace, insert or delete, with the names of the readers who made it. Nothing in the document changes until a person decides. This page calls that person the owner.
Vault.proofread(doc_id, readers) has each reader read the pages, then files the changes. A change that at least agree readers (2 by default) make identically has the state proposed. A change that fewer readers make has the state doubt. A reader named twice counts once. The owner then works through the review queue with these methods:
A change filed against an older version of its page cannot be accepted. accept raises an error that asks for a new proofread. A person can undo an accept only while its page has not changed since. edit_change, undo_decision and revert_page are for a person only. They raise PermissionError when called with by='agent'.
proof_md writes the record of a proofread as markdown, page by page. It lists what changed, what is proposed, what is in doubt and what was not taken.

title: proof
text:
Word changes
word_changes(a, b) compares two texts word by word. It returns each run of words that b replaces, inserts or deletes, as {at, n, before, after}. at is the index of the first word in a. n is the number of words of a that the change replaces (0 for an insertion). before and after are the words themselves.
apply_changes applies a list of such changes from the last to the first. It keeps the spacing and line breaks of the text everywhere else.
A stored page also has blocks, and the blocks must match its text. block_changes applies each change to the block that holds its words. It splits a change that crosses the end of a block. The cells of a table and the ## of a heading stay as read. change_box finds the box of the block that holds a change. A review screen uses it to show the change on the page image.

test_eq([b['text'] for b in block_changes(_bl, _tx, word_changes(_tx, '## Title here\n\none two three\n\nfour five'))], ['Title here', 'one two three', 'four five'])

text:
Proofreading
readers are model ids. chats maps a reader to a stand-in callable. The tests use it to run without models.
Each reader reads the page image through read_page, so the privacy rules are the rules of read_page. A reader that may not see a page skips it, and blocked reports the skip. A hosted reader may not see a Personal page without allow=True. No hosted reader sees a Local only page. The vault writes each hosted reading to the send log.
A second run of proofread replaces the open changes (proposed and doubt) on each page it reads. It leaves decided changes alone. A change keeps the box of the block that holds it when the blocks of the page have boxes.
progress(done, total, page, route, cost) is called once with done=0 and again after each page. If it returns False, the rest of the pages are not read. The result carries cancelled, unread and the summed cost.

title: vishalakshi
text:
vishalakshi keeps what you collect in one SQLite file on your own machine. The file is called a vault. You search the vault and ask it questions. One question can draw on a paper, a web page, a talk transcript, your own notes and source code on disk. The answer cites the sections it used.
vishalakshi is built from smaller packages. fossick fetches pages, papers and videos. litesearch stores the text and finds it again by keyword and by meaning. A Vault is a litesearch Index, and its search defaults come from litesearch. Urai is the chat interface the vault uses to talk to models. Rishi supplies the model backends. kosha indexes source code. rgapi searches files on disk that no index covers yet. rahasya finds personal information. varga recognises the kind of a document.

add takes a directory, a file or a piece of text. grab takes almost anything else, such as an arXiv id, a YouTube link, a GitHub repository, a PDF or a web address. It reads each kind in the way that suits it (acquire). Adding a source that is already in the vault reads it again only when its content changed. The changed field of the result says whether it did. note writes your own note. A note with a key= or a title replaces the earlier note with the same key or title. A note with neither is added as a new note.
Every search result also has the fields age and stale. age is the number of seconds since the document was filed. stale is True when the vault believes the document no longer matches its source. Stale results sort last. poll() (below) marks a document stale in three cases: a file changed or vanished, a web page is past its time limit and no watch refreshes it, or a watch has replaced it with a newer copy. poll() deletes only documents that are both stale and replaced.

title: vishalakshi
text:
Personal information and junk
A personal vault holds things that should not leave your machine, such as invoices, letters and bank statements. vishalakshi looks for personal information in everything it stores. It uses patterns and checksums and does not use a model. It finds email addresses, phone numbers, card and account numbers, national identity numbers, street addresses, dates of birth and API keys. On a held-out test set of 240 generated documents it missed nothing and raised no false alarm (evals/RESULTS.md). Names are harder. It finds only names that follow a title such as Dr or Mrs, and only when name detection is on (ner=True). The scanned_ner field of a report says whether name detection ran.
What it finds sets the privacy level of each document. The levels are Open, Personal and Local only. A document is Personal when an identifier was found or someone marked it. A document is Local only when someone set it by hand or when its type is sensitive, such as a passport or a payslip. Each shelf can also have a floor, a level that none of its documents goes below. A hosted model is a model that runs anywhere except this machine. Before every model call the vault decides with send_check what each document may give a hosted model. An Open document goes whole. A Personal document goes masked, or does not go. A Local only document never goes. A document’s title, headings and source path follow the same rule as its text. A model on this machine may read everything. The vault records each send to a hosted model in its send log. The details are on pii.
Junk is a separate problem. Cookie banners and site footers match every search and answer nothing. suggest_noisy ranks likely junk without labels (0.988 AUC on the test corpora). mark_noisy takes a document out of search (quality).

from vishalakshi.pii import pii_report

pii= in ask
what happens when the retrieved sections hold personal information




local
a model on this machine answers and is told never to repeat a personal detail. If the model is not local, nothing is sent


redact
each recognised identifier is masked, then the named model answers, hosted or not. The heading, title and source of each section are masked with its text. Names without a title are not masked


refuse
no model is asked. The result says what was held back



The default is local when a local runtime is installed, and redact when not. ask cannot run with detection off. pii='off' gives a warning and ask applies the default. The policy field of the result says which policy was used. The answer has any identifier that the model repeats masked. Under every policy a hosted model receives a Local only section as a placeholder only, with no heading, title or source. Search and reading also take pii= (off, redact or refuse). There the default is off, which returns the stored text. The MCP server defaults to redact for every tool and refuses off, because its client is a model that the vault does not run.

Watches and the queue
A watch repeats an acquisition on a schedule. Its action is an acquisition method (url, web, harvest, arxiv, youtube, crawl or path), remind to write a note, or folder. kind= is another name for action=. A folder watch keeps a snapshot of a directory. When it fires, it reports what was added, changed or removed, with its instructions for the person who reviews the change. A schedule is every='6h' or cron='0 9 * * 1'. pobblebonk keeps the schedules in the vault file.
poll() is the tick to call from cron or from the timer of an app. It returns jobs whose worker died to the queue, queues the watches that are due, runs the queue, and runs housekeep every ten minutes. A failed fetch is retried with a growing delay. After five attempts the job is set aside as dead. jobs(state='dead') lists dead jobs. See jobs.

text:
Books and scans
A scanned book has no usable text layer. An old print set in a legacy font can have a text layer that reads as gibberish. read_doc reads a PDF or a page image page by page. With parse='auto' it picks a route for each page. It keeps a text layer that passes its checks. It runs OCR on a scanned page. It sends a page that is still scanned, or that is flagged as garbled, to a vision model, local or hosted. preset= picks the reading prompt (generic, sanskrit, tamil or tables). hint= adds a sentence about the book. Given a folder, read_doc reads every PDF and image under it. It keeps the text, route and flags of each page as numbered versions. Reading a page again with a better model (reparse) never loses the earlier reading. A page image cannot be masked. A Personal page goes to a hosted model only with allow=True. A Local only page never goes. CachedChat records readings and replays them. A page with no recording reaches a model only when $VISHALAKSHI_RECORD_CHAT is set or a chat= is passed (read).
proofread has other models read the pages again. It files the word changes that each reading would make. A change that two readers agree on is proposed. A change that only one reader makes is in doubt. Nothing changes until the owner decides. accept applies changes as a new version of the page. reject sets changes aside. undo_decision and revert_page reverse decisions (proof).

v.read_doc('books/', parse='auto', model='claude/sonnet', preset='sanskrit', hint='verses end in ॥ n ॥')

v.pages(doc)                                   # text, route (text, ocr, model, proof), flags, version
v.reparse(doc, pages=[3, 4], model='claude/opus')
v.proofread(doc, ['claude/sonnet', 'gemini/gemini-2.5-pro'])
v.changes(doc, 'proposed'); v.accept(doc); print(v.proof_md(doc))

title: jobs
text:
Fetching a page, ingesting a batch of files and rebuilding the topic map can fail or stop part way. Queue keeps such work as rows in a jobs table in the vault’s own SQLite file. A job outlives the process that queued it. No separate server is needed.
enqueue adds a job. A worker takes jobs with claim. claim marks the jobs as running and gives the worker a lease, which is a time limit on the claim (lease, 10 minutes by default). Two workers that claim at the same time never get the same job.
If a worker dies, its lease runs out. reclaim then fails the job with the error lease expired. This counts as one attempt.
A job that fails runs again after a delay. The delay doubles with each failure, from 30 seconds up to 6 hours. After max_attempts failures (5 by default) the job is dead. A dead job stays in the table with its error, for a person to examine.
The queue lives in the same file as the documents. A job queued inside a write_txn is committed with the write that caused it. Queue needs only a database and knows nothing about a vault. acquire registers the vault’s own jobs on it.
source

    attempt:int, # failures so far; 1 on the first
    base:float=30, # first delay, seconds
    cap:float=21600, # longest delay, 6h
    jitter:float=0.25, # +/- fraction of the delay; spreads out jobs that failed together
)->float:
The delay before the next attempt: base seconds doubled for each failure so far, at most cap, with some random jitter.

):

title: jobs
text:
The queue
A job has a kind, which names the handler that runs it, and a payload, a dict stored as JSON. key makes queueing idempotent. While a job with the same kind and key is waiting or running, enqueue returns that job and adds no second one. A repeated fan-out does not double the work. A job with a lower priority number runs first.


source

Queue
def Queue(
    db, # open litesearch/fastlite Database; the queue lives in its file
    lease:float=600, # seconds a claim is held before another worker may take the job
    max_attempts:int=5, # attempts before a job is dead-lettered
    base:float=30, # first retry delay; doubles per attempt
    keep:float=604800, # how long finished jobs and run history survive `purge`, 7d
    busy_ms:int=30000, # lock wait before a write gives up; apsw's stock default is 100ms
):
A job queue stored in an open litesearch database, which runs every job at least once.

    kind:str, payloads, **kw
)->fastcore.foundation.L:
Enqueue many jobs of one kind in a single transaction.




source

Queue.enqueue
def enqueue(
    kind:str, # which handler runs it
    payload:dict=None, # arguments, stored as JSON
    run_at:float=None, # epoch seconds; defaults to now
    priority:int=0, # lower runs first
    key:str=None, # idempotency key: an identical key still ready or running wins
    max_attempts:int=None
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
Add one job, or return the waiting or running job that already has this key.



Claiming
claim picks and marks its jobs in one SQL statement. SQLite runs one write at a time. No other worker can take a job between the pick and the mark. Every job that claim returns is already running and already leased.
ack (finished) and fail (failed) count only while the job is still running under the caller’s worker name. Each worker needs its own name. A handler slower than lease loses its job to reclaim, and another worker can claim it. Without this check, the late ack could mark as done a job that another worker is still running. The late fail could send a finished job back for a third run. A late call returns the job with the state lost, and the run history records lost.


source

def reclaim(
    now:float=None
)->fastcore.foundation.L:
Fail each running job whose lease expired with lease expired; this counts one attempt, and the job is dead after max_attempts.




source

Queue.fail
def fail(
    job, # the claimed job
    error:str, # what went wrong; truncated to 500 chars on the row
    after:float=None, # seconds until the retry; None uses `backoff`
    dead:bool=False, # dead-letter now, whatever the attempts left: retrying a 401 never turns into success
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
Record a failure and schedule a retry after the backoff delay, or mark the job dead once its attempts are spent.




source

Queue.ack
def ack(
    job
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
Mark a claimed job done, or return it as lost when this worker’s lease was reclaimed.




source

Queue.claim
def claim(
    worker:str='worker', # who is holding the lease; recorded on the row and in history
    n:int=1, # how many jobs to take
    now:float=None
)->fastcore.foundation.L:
Claim up to n due jobs in one statement; no job was claimed twice over 400 jobs and 8 processes (evals/jobs.py).




Running
A handler is a function fn(payload). Register it with register or the on decorator. run_one runs one claimed job. drain claims and runs jobs until the queue is empty or limit jobs have run. A cron job calls drain. The way a handler ends sets what happens to the job:



the handler

is retried after Retry.after seconds or the backoff delay, and uses one attempt. Use it for work that did not fail but must run again, such as a page behind a bot wall

Use Terminal for a failure that waiting cannot fix, such as a 401, a model name that does not exist or a file that is gone. Without it, the default schedule retries a doomed job for most of a day. A job whose kind has no handler is dead at once, for the same reason.

)->fastcore.foundation.L:

Register the handler for kind.

jobs lists jobs by state and kind. pending counts the jobs that are waiting or running. stats counts the jobs in each state. history lists past runs.
dead lists the dead jobs with the error that ended each one. A failure deletes nothing. retry puts a dead job back on the queue and resets its attempt count. purge deletes finished jobs and run history older than keep (7 days by default). purge leaves dead jobs alone.

title: ask
section: Deciding what a model may be sent
text:
Deciding what a model may be sent
send_check runs before anything goes to a model. For each document, page or piece of text, it decides one of three outcomes: whole, masked, or withheld. Withheld means not sent.
send_check returns the decisions in rows, and the subsets send, masked and withheld. It also returns a why sentence for a person to read before the send. An example is gpt-4.1-nano, hosted. 1 personal document masked, 1 document open, 1 local-only document withheld.
send_rule holds the rule:

A model on this machine receives everything whole. model_local decides which models are local. LiteRT, MLX and llama.cpp are always local. Ollama is local only when $OLLAMA_HOST points at this machine. Every other runtime is hosted. A chat that names no runtime is hosted.
An Open item goes whole to any model.
A Local only item is withheld from a hosted model under every policy. allow=True does not change this.
Under redact, a Personal item goes to a hosted model masked. Under local and refuse, it is withheld.
A page image cannot be masked. A Personal page image is withheld from a hosted model under every policy except off, and when allow=True.
allow=True allows once. It sends Personal items whole for that one call, as policy='off' does.

ask, explain, categorize, extract, read_doc, reparse and proofread all decide through this rule. The decision covers everything that goes with the text. A document’s title, headings and source path are masked or withheld with it. A page image is read with the document’s title in its prompt. send_check judges the title with the page.
build_graph sends every chunk to its chat with nothing to mask. connect calls build_graph. A hosted chat builds the graph only when every document on the shelf is Open. Otherwise build_graph sends nothing and the result says why.
Masking replaces only what the detector recognises. A document marked Personal by hand, with nothing recognisable in it, goes to a hosted model under redact exactly as stored.
The send_log table of the vault records each send to a hosted model. A row has the time, the document and pages, the model and runtime, the policy, and the kinds of personal information when known. sends(ref) reads the log, newest first. The log has no row for a send to a local model or for a withheld item.

text:
When the sections hold personal information
pii explains the detector and the marks. The cells below show what ask does with them. They use a stand-in chat that records everything it receives. A leak appears as a recorded call.
The check runs on the chat that ask built, before ask sends anything. The next cell passes a hosted chat under the default local policy. ask does not call the model.

_seen.clear()
r = _v.ask('what is on invoice 4471?', mk_chat=_chat('remote', 'THIS MUST NEVER BE SENT'))
test_eq(_seen, {})                       # the model was never called at all
test_eq(r.refused, True)
r.answer

'held back: these sections hold personal information (card, email, phone) and remote is not a local runtime, so nothing was sent to it'


With a local runtime, ask sends the private sections to the local model under PII_SP. PII_SP tells the model to answer with counts, kinds and totals instead of personal details, and to say what it held back.

_seen.clear()
r = _v.ask('what is on invoice 4471?', mk_chat=_chat('litert',
    'One invoice, 240.00 GBP, due in September. Holding back the name, email, phone and card. '
    'Tell me what you need: a total, a due date, or a yes/no.'))
test_eq(_seen['runtime'], 'litert')
test_eq(_seen['sp'], PII_SP)             # not VAULT_SP: that one tells it to cite, and a citation points at the text
test_eq(r.get('refused', False), False)
r.answer

'One invoice, 240.00 GBP, due in September. Holding back the name, email, phone and card. Tell me what you need: a total, a due date, or a yes/no.'


instruction= sends a follow-up turn. When the local model holds something back, it names an instruction that would let it answer, such as “give me the total and the due date”. The caller sends that instruction with the same question.

_seen.clear()
r = _v.ask('what is on invoice 4471?', instruction='Give me the total and the due date only.',
           mk_chat=_chat('litert', 'Total 240.00 GBP, due 2026-09-01.'))
test_eq('Instruction from the questioner' in _seen['prompt'], True)
r.answer

'Total 240.00 GBP, due 2026-09-01.'


ask scans every answer over private sections again before it returns the answer. It masks identifiers that the model repeated, and leaked lists their kinds.

_seen.clear()
r = _v.ask('what is on invoice 4471?',
           mk_chat=_chat('litert', 'It is for ada@example.com, card 4111 1111 1111 1111.'))
test_eq(r.answer, 'It is for [EMAIL], card [CARD].')
r.leaked

{'email': 1, 'card': 1}

r = _v.ask('what is on invoice 4471?', pii='redact', mk_chat=_chat('remote', 'An invoice for 240.00 GBP [1]'))
test_eq('ada@example.com' in _seen['prompt'], False)
test_eq(_seen['runtime'], 'remote')
r.answer

'An invoice for 240.00 GBP [1]'


ask scrubs the fields of a structured answer (schema=) in the same way. An API key counts as personal information, as an email address does. A hosted chat is refused for a section that holds an API key, and for a document marked by hand.

title: code
text:
An index built for prose is a poor fit for source code. The useful units of code are functions and classes. The useful names are identifiers. What matters is which function calls which. kosha is the code index of the vault. It splits source files into functions and classes with their syntax tree. It embeds them with a model trained on code. It builds a call graph in which each symbol has a PageRank score, a measure of how central the symbol is. kosha keeps its index in .kosha/ inside the repository. It does not keep the index in the vault file.
index_code(dir) builds or updates that index. Later calls index only the files that changed. code_search searches the index. symbol(name) returns one function or class with its file, PageRank, callers and callees. where_to_add(description) ranks the places in the repository where a described change belongs.

title: quality
text:
The Beta prior
doc_prior turns the log into a multiplier on the retrieval score of each document. It models the usefulness of a document as a Beta distribution. The weighted wins and losses of the document update the distribution. A document with little evidence stays near neutral. A document cited once does not move far ahead.
gamma sets how strongly the prior changes a score. explore is the chance, from 0 to 1, that doc_prior samples from the distribution (Thompson sampling) and does not use its mean. Sampling keeps documents with little evidence in play. lo and hi clamp every multiplier, so no amount of evidence can bury a document.

title: quality
text:
The ranker
The ranker is a pairwise linear model trained on the feedback log. For each question it learns which of two sections ranks higher. fit_ranker(save=True) fits the ranker and stores it. use_ranker(True) is a separate call. It makes context use the ranker, and ask uses context. The ranker is off by default. In the measurements no learned reranker beat plain reciprocal rank fusion in a repeatable way.

The features
PAIR_FEATURES are the signals that exist when a section is retrieved. They are the retrieval score and rank, the gap to the top score, the words the section shares with the question (raw and weighted by rarity), the cosine similarity to the question, the section length, the document prior, the kind and age of the document, and the noise features. The method is in evals/.

title: pii
text:
Personal information, called PII below, is text that identifies a person or opens one of their accounts. Examples are an email address, a phone number, a card or bank account number, a national identity number such as a UK National Insurance number or an Indian Aadhaar number, a street address, a date of birth, an API key and a password. The detector is a separate package, rahasya. It uses patterns and checksums and no model. A card number must pass the Luhn check, and an NHS number must pass its mod-11 check. The detector gives the same answer on every run and downloads nothing. On a held-out test set of 240 generated documents it missed nothing and raised no false alarm (evals/RESULTS.md, section 3).
The detector does not find names on their own. No pattern describes a name. Name detection is a second pass, and it finds only a name that follows a title such as Mr, Dr or Prof. “Dr Charles Babbage” is found. “Ada Lovelace” with no title is not. The pass runs when a document is added, except on code, where identifiers are not names. It runs by default in ask (pii_ner=True). Vault.pii and gated run it only with ner=True, and the retrieval methods run it only with pii_ner=True. When a document holds personal information that the detector cannot see, a person marks the document, as described below.
This page covers the parts that need a vault: the marks a person sets, the privacy level of each document, the table of findings, and gated, which applies a policy to what search and reading return. ask describes what ask and the other model calls send to a model.

title: pii
section: Checking a document, and gating retrieval
text:
Checking a document, and gating retrieval
Vault.pii(ref) reports on one whole document: whether it holds personal information, which kinds, and whether a person’s mark overrides the detector. detected is the detector’s verdict. override is the mark. mark_pii marks a document as personal when the detector finds nothing, for example a letter that names people without titles. mark_not_pii clears a false alarm, such as your own invoice. Only a person may clear a mark (see the next section). pii_ctx runs the detector over every section of an assembled context, which is the result of context. ask decides on that report.
Retrieval methods apply the same policy to their results. search, sections, context, read, document, toc, doc_context and federate all take pii=. It sets what happens to a row that holds personal information:







pii=
the row’s text becomes




off, the default in Python and the CLI
the stored text; nothing is checked


redact
the stored text with each recognised identifier replaced by its kind, as in [EMAIL]


refuse
a placeholder such as [withheld: personal information (card, email)]



Under redact and refuse the row stays in the results. Its title and breadcrumb are masked, not removed. A pii key names the kinds found. A caller can use it to say why the text was held back. Three cases depend on the levels described in the next section.

A Local only document is withheld under redact as well as refuse. Its title, breadcrumb and source are withheld too.
A document that is private only because of a mark or the shelf’s floor, and that holds nothing the detector recognises, passes through redact unchanged. There is nothing to mask. Use refuse for such a document.
A document that a person cleared with mark_not_pii comes back untouched, unless the shelf’s floor is above Open.

The MCP server hands its results to a model that the vault does not run. Every MCP tool defaults to redact, and the server gates every result, including the result of ask. A client may ask for refuse. A client may not ask for off.

title: pii
text:
Privacy levels and findings
Every document has one of three privacy levels. The level sets what this package’s own model calls may send to a model that runs on another machine. This page calls such a model a hosted model.



level
how a document gets it
what a hosted model may be sent




Open (open)
nothing personal found, or a person cleared it
the text as it is


Personal (personal)
the detector found an identifier, or someone marked it
it depends on the policy: masked text, nothing, or with allow=True the whole text (see ask)


Local only (local)
someone set it with set_level, or its type is sensitive
nothing; only a model on this machine reads it



The sensitive types come from varga. They are passport, ID card, bank statement, payslip, tax return and clinical record. These rules cover what vishalakshi sends to models. They do not stop retrieval in Python or the CLI. read or search with the default pii='off' returns the text of a Local only document to the caller. The MCP server defaults to redact, which withholds that text.
level(ref) works out a document’s level in two steps.

A mark set with mark_pii, mark_not_pii or set_level decides the level. Without a mark, the level is the higher of the level of the document’s type and the level from its findings. Any identifier found in the text or the title makes the document Personal.
The result is raised to the shelf’s floor.

The floor is the lowest level any document on the shelf can have. set_floor sets it. A shelf for medical records can have a floor of Local only. A new document on that shelf is protected before the detector has found anything in it.
level(ref, page=n) gives the level of one page from the findings on that page. A page with no text takes the level of the whole document.
Anyone may raise a level. Only a person may lower one. These actions take by= and raise PermissionError unless by='person': set_level to a lower level, removing a mark, mark_not_pii, reject_pii, reset_pii and lowering a floor. The default is 'person'. Code that a person runs passes nothing. An agent passes its own name. The MCP server does not offer by. A model client cannot claim to be a person. It cannot turn the retrieval gate off with pii='off' either.
When a document is added, scan_pii scans each page. It files every identifier in the pii_findings table as a finding. A finding holds a kind, a page, the start and end offsets in the page text, and a fingerprint. The fingerprint is a 16-character hash of the kind and the value, with spacing, dashes and case removed. ADA@example.com and ada@example.com give the same fingerprint. 4111-1111-1111-1111 and 4111 1111 1111 1111 give the same fingerprint.
The table does not hold the value. The value is still in the document text, which the vault keeps as it was read. The hash has no secret key. Someone who hashes every possible short value, such as a date of birth, can recover it. Treat the findings table as private as the vault file. findings lists the findings. Each has a masked preview such as a••@e••••••.com, taken from the current page text.
A person can give a verdict on a finding. accept_pii confirms that a finding is personal. An agent may also call it, because it can only raise a level. reject_pii says that a finding is not personal. The level falls if nothing else holds it up. reset_pii takes a verdict back.
The vault stores a verdict against the fingerprint. The verdict covers every occurrence of the same value in the document. It survives a new read of the page. The new findings get new ids and keep the old verdict. A finding id from before the new read comes back as stale.

title: mcp
text:
MCP, the Model Context Protocol, is how AI assistants and editors call outside tools. vishalakshi-mcp is an MCP server that offers vault methods as tools. TOOLS lists them. Each tool is built with the cmd function that the command line uses. The arguments and the description of a tool are the arguments and the docstring of the method. The instructions of the server tell a model which tool to use first. context comes before answering a question. grab files something. note writes a conclusion back.
The server treats an MCP client as an agent and never as a person. Every tool that takes by is called with by='agent', and the server does not offer by. A client can raise a privacy level or mark a document personal. A client cannot clear a mark, reject a finding or lower a level (see pii).
The client is a model that the vault does not run. Every result passes through client_view before the client sees it. client_view withholds each string under a Local only document, including the title, headings and source. Every other string goes through redact, which masks the identifiers of a Personal document. A document that a person cleared with mark_not_pii comes back as stored. A tool that takes pii defaults to redact here. The CLI defaults to off. A client may ask for refuse, which withholds more. A client may not ask for off. Only a person can turn the gate off, as only a person can lower a level. ask returns no prompt. When a local model read a Local only section whole, its answer is also withheld. To use the server, add it to the configuration of the client:
The server talks over standard input and output by default. vishalakshi-mcp --http serves Streamable HTTP instead.

title: core
text:
A vault is one SQLite file that holds everything you have collected, such as web pages, papers, talk transcripts, PDFs, notes and source files. All of it is searchable together. Vault() opens the file $VISHALAKSHI_VAULT names, else ~/.vishalakshi/vault.db. Vault(path) opens or creates any other file. Vault(':memory:') makes a vault that lasts only as long as the process.
A Vault is a litesearch Index. litesearch decides how text is stored and found. Each thing you add becomes a document. litesearch splits a document along its headings into a tree of sections, which it calls nodes. It cuts the text of each section into chunks. It stores every chunk twice. One copy is text, for the full-text keyword search of SQLite. The other copy is a vector, a list of numbers from an embedding model. The model puts texts with similar meanings near each other. A search runs both lookups and merges the two rankings with reciprocal rank fusion (RRF). RRF scores each chunk by its rank in each list. It does not use the raw scores, because a keyword score and a vector distance cannot be compared. The default embedding model is potion-multilingual-128M. It is small and fast and covers over 100 languages, including Devanagari. encoder= picks another model (see concepts).
The vault adds these to litesearch:

text:
Shelves
One vault file can hold several shelves. A shelf is a separate collection with its own chunks, section tree and vector index. A large corpus on one shelf, such as a thousand papers, does not crowd a small shelf out of the rankings. shelf(name) opens a shelf and creates it the first time. A shelf keeps the embedding model it was first written with. Reopening it with a different model raises an error, because vectors from two models cannot be compared. shelves() lists the shelves with their models and document counts. drop_shelf deletes a shelf. The main shelf is called store. SHELVES names the shelves that the vault itself uses: store, papers, sanskrit, code and data. Acquisition sends some kinds to their own shelf through KIND_SHELF, below.

Marks
A mark is a judgement about one document. The doc_marks table keeps it when the document is added again. There are three marks. noisy is for junk such as a cookie banner or a site footer. search, sections, context and ask leave noisy documents out. pii_override holds the privacy marks described on pii. stale says that a document no longer matches its source. Search still returns a stale document, flagged and sorted last. The vault clears the mark when the document is added again with new content. mark sets any of them. mark_noisy, mark_stale and the pii methods are the named ways to set a mark. marks() lists every mark on the shelf. marks(ref) returns the mark on one document.

title: read
text:
Many PDFs carry a text layer, which is the text you can select and copy. A PDF made from a digital document has an exact text layer, and reading it costs nothing. A scanned PDF has no text layer, or it has one made by OCR (optical character recognition), which can be poor. Old books in Indian scripts are often worse. Many were set in legacy fonts. The text layer of such a font reads as Latin gibberish, or it splits apart akṣaras, the letter clusters of Devanagari. A vision model reads images, so it can read such a page from its picture. It costs time or money for every page, and it makes mistakes of its own.
read_doc decides page by page. The parse argument sets the route:
model is any model id that the urai package accepts, local or hosted, such as claude/sonnet or gemini/gemini-2.5-flash. None means the value of $VISHALAKSHI_MODEL.
There are two entry points. The function read_doc(path) reads one file and returns its pages. It does not use a vault. Vault.read_doc(src) reads a file, or every PDF and image under a folder, into the vault. Each file becomes one document. The vault keeps the text, route and flags of each page as numbered versions. A new reading of a page never removes an earlier reading.

title: read
text:
Prompts
A reading prompt tells a vision model what to return. PRESETS holds four reading prompts. Each asks for the page as JSON. The JSON is a list of items in reading order. An item is a heading, a paragraph of prose, a verse, a table, a note or a colophon, which is the line that closes a chapter in an Indian text. Each item has its text exactly as printed and any number printed with it. This page calls the items of a read page blocks.







preset
use




generic
any printed page


sanskrit
Sanskrit prints. It names the letters that old prints make easy to misread. It tells the model to leave out translation and commentary


tamil
Tamil prints. It names the letters that old prints make easy to misread


tables
tables, read as rows of cells



Every preset also asks for a box per item. The box is the region that the item covers, as [x0, y0, x1, y1], in fractions of the page width and height from the top left. An app can use it to crop the block out of the page image or to highlight it.
reading_prompt(name, title, script, hint) fills a preset with the title of the document, its script (Devanagari by default) and a hint. A hint is a sentence about this book, such as how it numbers its verses or what to skip. A name that is not one of the four presets is the whole prompt. reading_prompt fills {of}, {title}, {script} and {hint} in it. If the prompt has JSON braces that are not doubled, formatting fails and reading_prompt returns the prompt unchanged.

text:
Pages as images
A vision model receives a picture of the page. render draws one page of a PDF as a PNG at dpi (200 by default). Some hosted models refuse large images. When the PNG is larger than max_bytes (3 MB), render returns a JPEG with a long side of at most max_px (3,000 pixels). fit does the same for an image file.
Two cuts help with hard pages. halves splits a landscape image into a left page and a right page. A landscape image is usually a scan of two facing pages, called a spread. page_strips cuts a tall page into overlapping horizontal strips. The model then sees worn or small type at a larger scale.

text:
Checks
flags lists what looks wrong with a page’s text. It is how parse='auto' decides that a text layer cannot be trusted.







flag
meaning




thin
fewer than min_chars (20) letters, as on a scanned page


replacement
the Unicode replacement character, which marks text that failed to decode


legacy
more than 5 Latin-1 or typographic characters per 100 letters, which is how a legacy Devanagari font’s text layer reads


split
a line that starts with a vowel sign or virāma, a piece of an akṣara cut off from the rest


akshara
an akṣara that cannot be written, such as a virāma followed by a vowel sign


foreign
Greek or Cyrillic letters next to Devanagari



disagree(a, b) measures how far two readings of the same text differ: the letter edits between them divided by the letters in the longer one. Spaces, digits, daṇḍas and punctuation are ignored and vowel signs count. A value of 0.1 or more is worth a look.

title: read
text:
Reading a page
read_page sends one page image to a vision model. It returns blocks, their text joined as markdown (text), the model and the cost that the backend reported.
With no chat=, the call goes through CachedChat. CachedChat records each reading once and replays it later. A repeated read of the same page costs nothing. The recordings are in chatcache in the working directory, or in the folder that $VISHALAKSHI_CHAT_CACHE names. A page with no recording reaches the model only when $VISHALAKSHI_RECORD_CHAT is set. Otherwise read_page raises an error that says so. fresh=True drops the recorded reply and asks the model again. A reply that is not JSON raises an error and is not recorded, and the next try reaches the model. chat= takes any callable in place of a model. The tests use it to run without a model. fit limits the size of every image before it is sent.
A block keeps its box only when the box is four numbers that make a real rectangle. read_page clamps the box to the page. It drops any other box. crop cuts a block out of the page image by its box.
Before it sends an image, read_page asks send_rule whether the page may go. The level of the page is the level of its document. It rises to Personal when text holds an identifier. text is the text layer or the OCR text of the page. A page image cannot be masked. A Personal page goes to a hosted model only with allow=True or pii='off'. A Local only page never goes to a hosted model. A page that may not be sent comes back empty, and blocked says why.

title: read
text:
Reading a document
read_doc(path) takes a PDF or a page image and returns one row per page: {page, text, route, flags}. A page that the model read also has blocks, model and cost. route says where the text came from. Its values are text (the text layer), ocr, model, and scanned when nothing read the page. pages=[...] limits which pages may go to the model. The other pages keep their text layer. workers (4 by default) sets how many pages are read at the same time.
Privacy works page by page, as in read_page. When any page is going to a model and pii is not off, read_doc first checks the whole text layer for a sensitive doctype. A document whose text clearly reads as a passport or a payslip is Local only before any page image leaves. local_model= or a built local_chat= reads the pages that the hosted model may not read. Without either, those pages keep their text layer and carry blocked. A scanned page has no text to check. Only the level of its document applies to it.
These options control a long read:

progress(done, total, page, route, cost) is called once with done=0, then after each page that was due for the model. If it returns False, the reading stops. The pages not yet read keep their text layer or OCR. The result’s cancelled is True, and unread lists those pages. read_doc ignores an error raised inside progress.
cache= keeps each model reading as a JSON file, {page, items, cost, model}. The file is in a folder (p0001.json, or p0001a.json and p0001b.json for the two halves of a spread), or at the path that a function cache(page, half) returns. A cached page is not sent again. Its cost is None, because nothing was spent, and cached is True.
redo=[...] reads those pages again even when they are cached. After the new reading is saved, the old reading moves to a sibling folder. The folder has the name of the cache folder with _prev added. A number is added to the file name when an older copy is already there.
spread=True treats a landscape page as two facing pages and reads the halves in turn. strips=k sends each image as k overlapping strips.
clean= is a function that read_doc applies to the text of each block before it keeps the block.
tries=n tries a failing page up to n times. It waits RETRY_WAIT seconds (10) after the first failure, 20 after the second, and so on. A page that still fails keeps its text layer, carries its error, and is listed in the result’s failed. Without tries, read_doc raises the first error.

doc_cost(rows) adds up the cost of the pages that a model read. doc_files(folder) lists the PDFs and images under a folder.

text:
Into the vault
Vault.read_doc(src) reads a file, or every PDF and image under a folder. It adds each file to the vault as one document. Search and ask reach the document like any other. It also keeps each page as a version in the read_pages table. A page gets a new version only when its text, route or blocks changed. Reading a file twice with the same result adds nothing.
Each new version is scanned for personal information, and the findings are filed against it (see pii). A new document starts at the shelf’s floor. A document already in the vault keeps its own level.
Vault.pages(doc_id) returns the latest version of each current page. history=True returns every version of those pages. A shorter file marks pages beyond its end stale. Their readings remain in read_pages. They are not indexed or returned by default. The vault writes every page that a hosted model read to the send log.
Use stale=True on pages, search, sections, context, document, doc_context, ask or federate to include retained stale pages. Retrieval builds a temporary in-memory index for this request. It never adds stale text to the stored index. Hybrid search can still return unrelated current pages for a missing word.
prune_stale(doc_id=None, dry_run=False) deletes every reading of stale pages on this shelf. It returns each document id, page number and version count. dry_run=True returns the same report without deleting anything. The method is Python-only, like housekeep.
The result of Vault.read_doc is the ingest result with these keys added: routes (how many pages took each route), flagged, blocked, cost, model_pages, cancelled, unread and failed.
Vault.reparse(doc_id, pages=[...]) reads pages of a document again. By default it uses the model (parse='llm') and the preset, script and hint of the document. It files the new readings as new versions and re-indexes the document. Use it when a page came out badly and a better model should read it. reparse returns the ingest result with these keys added: pages (the pages it read), changed (the pages whose text changed), blocked, cost, model_pages, cancelled and unread.
Both methods take progress. A cancelled or failed read of a document already in the vault leaves its unread and failed pages as they were. When a folder is read with cache=, each file caches in its own subfolder. The subfolder has the file’s path below the folder, extension included, so a/report.pdf and b/report.pdf do not share one. A cache written by an earlier version, which named each file by its stem alone, is not reused. Those pages are read again.
